cases.n: Ferns Report — Diocese of Ferns
cases.victims_note: More than 100 allegations made between 1962 and 2002
cases.who: Catholic Diocese of Ferns
cases.cover: Bishop Herlihy moved accused priests to other posts or dioceses for a period, then reinstated them; Gardaí failed to record or properly investigate some pre-1988 complaints
cases.d: The state Ferns Inquiry, published 25 October 2005, examined more than 100 allegations of child sexual abuse made between 1962 and 2002 against 21 priests of the diocese. Bishop Donal Herlihy moved accused priests temporarily and then reinstated them, and ordained men he knew or should have known posed a risk. Bishop Brendan Comiskey never got a priest to stand aside from ministry. The report found Garda handling of one of eight formal complaints 'wholly inadequate' and some pre-1988 complaints were not recorded.
cases.cite: Ferns Inquiry report, 25 October 2005, as reported by RTÉ News

cases.n: Murphy Report — Archdiocese of Dublin
cases.victims_note: 320 people complained of abuse 1975–2004; a further 130 complaints after May 2004
cases.who: Catholic Archdiocese of Dublin
cases.cover: Abuse 'covered up' 1975–2004; bishops generally did not report to Gardaí before 1996; archdiocese took out insurance against abuse litigation from 1987; Gardaí knew of complaints against Fr Tony Walsh in 1990–91 and took no action
cases.d: The Commission of Investigation into the Catholic Archdiocese of Dublin reported on 26 November 2009. It examined a sample of 46 priests out of 102 within its remit; 320 people complained of abuse between 1975 and 2004. It found Archbishops McQuaid, Ryan, McNamara and Connell handled complaints badly and that the archdiocese had insured itself against abuse litigation from 1987. It also criticised the Gardaí, and the Garda Commissioner apologised.
cases.cite: Commission of Investigation, Report into the Catholic Archdiocese of Dublin (Murphy Report), 26 November 2009

cases.n: Cloyne Report — Diocese of Cloyne
cases.who: Catholic Diocese of Cloyne; Bishop John Magee
cases.cover: Nine complaints that should have gone to the Gardaí were not reported; none of the 1996–2008 complaints reported to the health service; Vatican's reaction to Irish guidelines described as 'entirely unhelpful'
cases.d: The Cloyne Report, published 13 July 2011, examined the diocese's handling of allegations against 19 clerics from 1996 to February 2009, after the Irish church had adopted reporting procedures. Nine complaints that should have been reported to the Gardaí were not, and none were reported to the health authorities. Bishop John Magee was found to have shown little interest in applying the guidelines for 12 years. The report said the Vatican's response to the Irish procedures allowed bishops to ignore them.
cases.cite: Commission of Investigation, Report into the Catholic Diocese of Cloyne, July 2011, as summarised by the Irish Times

cases.n: Ryan Commission — industrial schools run by religious orders
cases.victims_note: More than 30,000 children were sent to the institutions; redress scheme paid about 12,000 people
cases.who: Christian Brothers (most boys' institutions), Sisters of Mercy (most girls' institutions) and other Catholic orders
cases.cover: Christian Brothers sued the commission in 2004 to keep members' names out; no real names of perpetrators published; findings not to be used for prosecutions; state Department of Education inspections failed
cases.d: The Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse reported on 20 May 2009 after a nine-year investigation of more than 250 church-run institutions that held over 30,000 children from the 1930s to the 1990s. It found sexual abuse 'endemic' in boys' institutions run mainly by the Christian Brothers; the Sisters of Mercy ran most girls' institutions. The 2,600-page report names no perpetrators after a Christian Brothers lawsuit. A parallel state redress scheme paid about 12,000 people an average of €65,000.
cases.cite: Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse (Ryan Report), 20 May 2009, as reported by CBS News/AP

cases.n: Scoping Inquiry — abuse in religious-run schools
cases.victims_note: 2,395 allegations recorded; report says true number likely higher
cases.who: 42 religious orders that ran day and boarding schools
cases.d: The state Scoping Inquiry, published 3 September 2024, recorded 2,395 allegations of sexual abuse against 884 alleged abusers at 308 schools run by 42 religious orders, mostly from the 1960s to the 1990s. 590 allegations involving 190 alleged abusers concerned 17 special schools. More than half of the alleged abusers are dead. The government announced a full Commission of Investigation.
cases.cite: Report of the Scoping Inquiry into Historical Sexual Abuse in Day and Boarding Schools Run by Religious Orders, 3 September 2024

cases.n: Archdiocese of Boston — Spotlight 2002 and Massachusetts AG report 2003
cases.victims_note: At least 789 minors; AG estimated the true number probably exceeds 1,000
cases.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Boston; Cardinal Bernard Law
cases.cover: Accused priests reassigned with Cardinal Law's personal involvement; church alerted law enforcement only twice in six decades; bishops sought leniency for priests and withheld information from prosecutors
cases.d: After the Boston Globe Spotlight series beginning January 2002, Cardinal Law resigned in December 2002. The Massachusetts Attorney General's report of 23 July 2003 found at least 237 priests and 13 other church workers accused of abusing at least 789 minors over six decades, and 'overwhelming evidence' that Law knew and took part in reassigning abusers. No criminal statute allowed charging church leaders.
cases.cite: Office of the Massachusetts Attorney General, 'The Sexual Abuse of Children in the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Boston', 23 July 2003, as reported by the Boston Globe

cases.n: Pennsylvania grand jury — six dioceses
cases.place: Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, Allentown, Scranton, Greensburg, Erie
cases.victims_note: 'At least 1,000' identified; grand jury believed there were more
cases.who: Six Pennsylvania Catholic dioceses
cases.cover: Abusers moved and protected, some later promoted; reports brushed aside; most crimes beyond statute of limitations
cases.d: A 23-member statewide grand jury report released by Attorney General Josh Shapiro on 14 August 2018 identified 301 'predator priests' and at least 1,000 child victims over about 70 years in six dioceses. The roughly 1,400-page report found bishops 'went to great lengths to keep it secret' and moved abusers. Most crimes were too old to prosecute.
cases.cite: 40th Statewide Investigating Grand Jury report, 14 August 2018, as reported by America magazine

cases.n: Illinois Attorney General — clergy abuse report
cases.who: Six Catholic dioceses of Illinois
cases.cover: Before the investigation the dioceses had publicly listed only 103 substantiated abusers
cases.d: Attorney General Kwame Raoul's report of 23 May 2023, from an investigation opened in 2018, named 451 Catholic clerics and religious brothers who abused at least 1,997 children in Illinois' six dioceses over decades. Before the inquiry the dioceses had publicly listed 103 substantiated abusers.
cases.cite: Illinois Attorney General, Report on Catholic Clergy Child Sex Abuse in Illinois, 23 May 2023

cases.n: John Jay College study — US Catholic clergy 1950–2002
cases.place: United States (commissioned by US bishops, Washington DC)
cases.victims_note: 10,667 individuals reported abuse to bishops; authors say true number likely higher
cases.who: US Conference of Catholic Bishops (commissioned study)
cases.cover: Of accused priests whose cases reached police, only one in three was charged; 3% served prison time
cases.d: The John Jay College of Criminal Justice study, commissioned by the US bishops and released 27 February 2004, counted 4,392 priests and deacons (about 4% of clergy) accused of abusing 10,667 minors between 1950 and 2002. Reported abuse peaked in the 1970s; one-third of allegations were made only in 2002–03. 149 priests with more than 10 allegations each accounted for 27% of allegations. Costs to the church were put at $472 million at the time.
cases.cite: John Jay College, 'The Nature and Scope of Sexual Abuse of Minors by Catholic Priests and Deacons in the United States 1950–2002', 2004, as summarised by America magazine

cases.n: Maryland Attorney General — Archdiocese of Baltimore
cases.victims_note: 'Over 600' children; report says true number 'likely far higher'
cases.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Baltimore
cases.cover: Archdiocese often failed to report to authorities or remove abusers; some accused allowed to retire with support; post-2002 public list omitted known abusers
cases.d: The Maryland Attorney General's report, released in redacted form on 5 April 2023, identified 156 priests and others associated with the Archdiocese of Baltimore who abused more than 600 children over 80 years. Attorney General Anthony Brown described 'repeated coverup' by the church. A judge ordered the names and titles of 37 people redacted.
cases.cite: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Report on Child Sexual Abuse in the Archdiocese of Baltimore, 5 April 2023, as reported by Fortune/AP

cases.n: Missouri Attorney General — four Catholic dioceses
cases.who: Archdiocese of St. Louis and dioceses of Kansas City–St. Joseph, Jefferson City, Springfield–Cape Girardeau
cases.d: Attorney General Eric Schmitt reported on 13 September 2019 on a review, opened in August 2018, of records of more than 2,000 priests who served in Missouri since 1945. It found 163 credible allegations of abuse or misconduct against minors by diocesan priests and deacons; 83 of the accused had died and the statute of limitations had expired for 46 alleged crimes. Twelve former priests were referred for prosecution.
cases.cite: Missouri Attorney General's Office, clergy abuse report, 13 September 2019, as reported by NPR/KPBS

cases.n: Michigan Attorney General — clergy abuse investigation
cases.victims_note: 552 victims identified by December 2019; AG expected 'several thousand' by the end
cases.who: Catholic dioceses of Michigan
cases.d: Attorney General Dana Nessel said on 23 December 2019 that the state investigation had identified 270 priests alleged to have abused 552 victims. Seven priests had been charged in 2019, two of whom had pleaded guilty. Most cases could not be prosecuted because of statutes of limitations.
cases.cite: Detroit News, 23 December 2019, reposted by BishopAccountability.org; Michigan AG press releases

cases.n: Archdiocese of Agaña — Archbishop Apuron and bankruptcy
cases.victims_note: More than 220 former altar boys, students and Boy Scouts sued
cases.who: Archdiocese of Agaña; former Archbishop Anthony Apuron
cases.d: A Vatican tribunal of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith found former Archbishop Anthony Apuron guilty of some charges including sexual abuse of minors in March 2018; the appeal was rejected in February 2019. He was barred from office and from living in Guam but not laicised; he denies the allegations. The archdiocese filed for bankruptcy in January 2019 facing more than 200 lawsuits naming 35 clergy, teachers and scoutmasters. Guam lifted the civil statute of limitations in 2016.
cases.cite: Catholic News Agency/EWTN News, 8 August 2019; America magazine, 9 November 2018

cases.n: Mount Cashel Orphanage — Hughes Royal Commission
cases.who: Congregation of Christian Brothers, Mount Cashel Orphanage
cases.cover: Inquiry found officials transferred offenders and covered up the abuse; insufficient evidence to charge church and government officials with obstruction
cases.d: The provincial Royal Commission led by Samuel Hughes (begun 1 June 1989, reported 1991–92) examined abuse of boys by Christian Brothers at Mount Cashel orphanage, which closed in 1990, and the justice system's response. It found officials had transferred offenders and covered up the abuse. Eleven Christian Brothers were convicted, with sentences from 4 months to 11 years. The Brothers apologised in April 1992; the Newfoundland government paid $11.5 million in 1996.
cases.cite: Royal Commission of Inquiry into the Response of the Newfoundland Criminal Justice System to Complaints (Hughes Inquiry), 1991–92

cases.n: Winter Commission — Archdiocese of St. John's
cases.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of St. John's; Archbishop Alphonsus Penney
cases.cover: Report assigned Archbishop Penney part of the blame for covering up abuse
cases.d: Archbishop Alphonsus Penney commissioned former Lieutenant Governor Gordon Winter in May 1989 to inquire into sexual abuse of children by clergy of the archdiocese. The 1990 report assigned Penney part of the blame for covering up abuse, and he resigned after its release.
cases.cite: Report of the Archdiocesan Commission of Enquiry into the Sexual Abuse of Children by Members of the Clergy (Winter Report), 1990

cases.n: Cornwall Public Inquiry
cases.who: Roman Catholic Diocese of Alexandria-Cornwall, local police and other institutions
cases.d: Ontario's Cornwall Public Inquiry, established 14 April 2005 under Commissioner G. Normand Glaude, examined how institutions including the Catholic diocese and local police responded to child sexual abuse allegations against adults in positions of trust, including Catholic clergy. Its 2009 report found systemic failures in the justice system's response. The commissioner declined to make a finding on whether a child-abuse ring existed, saying it was outside the mandate. The inquiry cost $53 million.
cases.cite: Report of the Cornwall Inquiry, December 2009

cases.n: Royal Commission — Catholic Church data, Australia
cases.victims_note: 4,444 people reported abuse at more than 1,000 Catholic institutions (claims 1980–2015)
cases.who: Catholic Church in Australia, incl. St John of God Brothers (40.4% of brothers accused)
cases.d: Data presented to the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse on 6 February 2017 showed 4,444 people reported abuse to Catholic authorities between 1980 and 2015, at more than 1,000 institutions, naming 1,880 alleged perpetrators. About 7% of priests who served between 1950 and 2010 were alleged perpetrators; 40.4% of St John of God Brothers were accused. Religious brothers (32%) and priests (30%) were the largest groups. The commission referred 309 cases to police.
cases.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Case Study 50 data, 6 February 2017, as reported by NPR

cases.n: Diocese of Ballarat — Gerald Ridsdale and Royal Commission Case Study 28
cases.victims_note: Convicted of abusing more than 70 children; advocates estimate hundreds
cases.who: Catholic Diocese of Ballarat; Bishop Ronald Mulkearns
cases.cover: Ridsdale moved through about 13 postings 1962–1991; Mulkearns knew by late 1975; a senior police officer in 1972 offered a detective promotion to stop investigating Monsignor John Day
cases.d: Gerald Ridsdale, ordained 1961, was convicted in a series of trials from 1993 of abusing more than 70 children; he died in prison in 2025. He was moved between parishes including Mildura, Swan Hill, Warrnambool, Apollo Bay, Edenhope and Mortlake, then to Sydney. The Royal Commission's Ballarat report of 6 December 2017 found Bishop Mulkearns knew of his offending by late 1975 and still reappointed him, a 'catastrophic' failure. It also found police obstruction of a 1972 investigation of Monsignor John Day.
cases.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Report of Case Study 28 (Ballarat), December 2017; The Courier (Ballarat)

cases.n: Cardinal George Pell — convicted 2018, acquitted 2020
cases.who: Cardinal George Pell (former Archbishop of Melbourne, Vatican treasurer)
cases.d: A Melbourne jury convicted Cardinal George Pell in December 2018 on five charges relating to two choirboys at St Patrick's Cathedral in 1996. On 7 April 2020 the High Court of Australia unanimously quashed the convictions and entered acquittals; he had served more than 400 days in prison. Separately, Royal Commission findings released in May 2020 said Pell was aware of abuse by clergy in the 1970s; he disputed this. He died in 2023.
cases.cite: Pell v The Queen [2020] HCA 12, 7 April 2020, as reported by 1News

cases.n: Royal Commission into Abuse in Care — Catholic institutions
cases.victims_note: About 200,000 abused across all state and faith-based care 1950–2019 (not Catholic alone); church data showed 14% of NZ clergy accused 1950–1999
cases.who: Catholic Church in Aotearoa New Zealand; St John of God Brothers at Marylands School
cases.cover: Church relied on psychiatrists' opinions to transfer abusers to other ministries where they reoffended; commission recommended investigating priests transferred to Papua New Guinea
cases.d: The Royal Commission's final report, Whanaketia, published 24 July 2024, found about 200,000 people were abused in state and faith-based care from 1950 to 2019. It found Catholic responses inadequate, noting a 2020 church briefing that 14% of clergy were accused over 1950–1999, and singled out Marylands School in Christchurch for some of the highest levels of sexual abuse. It found abusers were transferred to other ministries and recommended an inquiry into priests sent to Papua New Guinea.
cases.cite: Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care, Whanaketia, 24 July 2024, as reported by EWTN/CNA

cases.n: IICSA — Roman Catholic Church in England and Wales
cases.victims_note: More than 900 complaints involving over 3,000 instances of abuse, 1970–2015
cases.who: Catholic Church in England and Wales; Cardinal Vincent Nichols
cases.cover: Accused priests reassigned to other parishes; Holy See and Apostolic Nuncio refused to provide a witness statement
cases.d: The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse reported on 10 November 2020 that the Church in England and Wales received more than 900 complaints involving over 3,000 instances of child sexual abuse between 1970 and 2015, with more than 100 allegations a year since 2016. It found the church put its reputation before children and criticised Cardinal Nichols. The Holy See declined to provide a witness statement.
cases.cite: IICSA, The Roman Catholic Church: Safeguarding in the Roman Catholic Church in England and Wales, 10 November 2020

cases.n: IICSA — Ampleforth and Downside Benedictine schools
cases.who: English Benedictine Congregation — Ampleforth Abbey and Downside Abbey schools
cases.cover: Both institutions for decades avoided giving police and social services information; 'tell them nothing' approach after 2001
cases.d: The IICSA report of 9 August 2018 found a culture of acceptance of abuse at Ampleforth and Downside, where children as young as seven and eleven were abused over about four decades. Ten people linked to the schools, mostly monks, were convicted or cautioned for sexual or indecent-image offences. Both abbeys tried for decades to avoid passing information to police and social services.
cases.cite: IICSA, Ampleforth and Downside (English Benedictine Congregation case study), 9 August 2018; RTÉ

cases.n: IICSA — Archdiocese of Birmingham
cases.victims_note: More than 130 allegations
cases.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Birmingham
cases.cover: Fr James Robinson moved parish after 1980s complaints, police not told; he fled to the US in 1985 and received archdiocesan payments for seven years; the Vicar General helped Fr Samuel Penney avoid arrest and leave the UK
cases.d: The IICSA case study report of 20 June 2019 found more than 130 allegations against 78 people associated with the archdiocese since the 1930s. It examined priests James Robinson, Samuel Penney and John Tolkien. Robinson was moved to another parish after complaints in the 1980s without police being told, then fled to the US in 1985 while still receiving archdiocesan support; he was later extradited and jailed for 21 years.
cases.cite: IICSA, Archdiocese of Birmingham Investigation Report, 20 June 2019

cases.n: Deetman Commission — Catholic Church in the Netherlands
cases.victims_note: 'Several tens of thousands' of children had unwanted sexual contact with church officials (survey estimate; other coverage cites 10,000–20,000)
cases.who: Catholic dioceses and religious orders in the Netherlands
cases.cover: Policy of 'not hanging out the dirty washing'; bishops and officials knew and did not act
cases.d: The commission led by former minister Wim Deetman, set up by the church in March 2010, reported on 16 December 2011. It identified at least 800 priests, monks and other religious who abused children between 1945 and 1985, 105 of them still alive, and estimated tens of thousands of victims. It found bishops and officials knew of the abuse and followed a policy of avoiding scandal.
cases.cite: Commissie-Deetman, 'Seksueel misbruik van minderjarigen in de Rooms-Katholieke Kerk', 16 December 2011, as reported by DutchNews.nl

cases.n: Adriaenssens commission and Vangheluwe resignation, Belgium
cases.victims_note: 475 complaints in the first half of 2010; 13 suicides reported
cases.who: Catholic Church in Belgium, about 29 religious orders; Bishop Roger Vangheluwe of Bruges
cases.cover: Judicial raid in June 2010 seized the commission's files (later ruled disproportionate); commission members resigned
cases.d: Bishop Roger Vangheluwe of Bruges resigned in April 2010 after admitting he abused his nephew from 1973 to 1986. The church-backed commission led by psychiatrist Peter Adriaenssens received 475 complaints in six months; its report of 10 September 2010 recorded 13 suicides linked to clerical abuse and 102 verified alleged abusers in about 29 orders. In June 2010 police raided church premises and seized the commission's files (Operation Chalice/Kelk); an appeals court later ruled the raids disproportionate.
cases.cite: Commission for the Treatment of Complaints of Sexual Abuse in a Pastoral Relationship (Adriaenssens report), 10 September 2010, as reported by RTÉ

cases.n: MHG study — German Bishops' Conference
cases.who: German Catholic dioceses
cases.cover: Researchers found personnel files had been destroyed or manipulated
cases.d: The study by researchers from Mannheim, Heidelberg and Giessen, commissioned by the German Bishops' Conference and presented on 25 September 2018, found 1,670 clerics (4.4% of clergy) accused of abusing 3,677 minors between 1946 and 2014. The authors called the figures conservative and found that personnel files had been destroyed or manipulated.
cases.cite: MHG study, 'Sexueller Missbrauch an Minderjährigen durch katholische Priester, Diakone und männliche Ordensangehörige', 25 September 2018, as reported by JURIST

cases.n: Munich and Freising abuse report (Westpfahl Spilker Wastl)
cases.victims_note: At least 497 (247 male, 182 female, 68 unassigned)
cases.who: Archdiocese of Munich and Freising; former archbishops incl. Joseph Ratzinger, Friedrich Wetter, Reinhard Marx
cases.cover: Report found misconduct by archdiocesan leaders, including Joseph Ratzinger in four cases; only 4 of 173 accused priests were dismissed from the clerical state
cases.d: The report commissioned by the archdiocese from law firm Westpfahl Spilker Wastl, published 20 January 2022, covered 1945–2019 and found at least 497 victims and 261 possible perpetrators and accomplices, 173 of them priests. It found misconduct by Joseph Ratzinger (Archbishop 1977–1982, later Pope Benedict XVI) in four cases, Cardinal Wetter in 21 and Cardinal Marx in three. Ratzinger corrected his statement that he had not attended a 15 January 1980 meeting about priest Peter Hullermann, who was admitted to Munich in 1980 and later reoffended.
cases.cite: Westpfahl Spilker Wastl, 'Sexueller Missbrauch Minderjähriger und erwachsener Schutzbefohlener durch Kleriker sowie hauptamtliche Bedienstete im Bereich der Erzdiözese München und Freising von 1945 bis 2019', 20 January 2022

cases.n: Peter Hullermann — transferred from Essen to Munich 1980
cases.who: Archdiocese of Munich and Freising; Diocese of Essen
cases.cover: Accused priest accepted into Munich for therapy in January 1980 with Cardinal Ratzinger's approval, then reassigned to pastoral work where he abused again; remained a priest until 2010
cases.d: In January 1980 the Munich archdiocese under Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger approved receiving Fr Peter Hullermann for therapy after accusations of abusing minors. He was then given pastoral work, abused minors again, and in June 1986 was convicted, fined DM4,000 and given an 18-month suspended sentence. He stayed a priest until suspended on 14 March 2010. Then vicar general Gerhard Gruber took responsibility for readmitting him.
cases.cite: Süddeutsche Zeitung reporting (2010) as cited in Wikipedia; Munich report 2022

cases.n: Regensburger Domspatzen choir — Weber report
cases.victims_note: 547 victims of physical and/or sexual violence, of whom 67 suffered sexual violence
cases.who: Regensburger Domspatzen cathedral choir and boarding schools, Diocese of Regensburg
cases.cover: Report faulted choir director Georg Ratzinger for 'looking away' and said former bishop Gerhard Ludwig Müller bore 'clear responsibility' for weaknesses in investigating
cases.d: Lawyer Ulrich Weber's final report of 18 July 2017 found 547 boys suffered physical and/or sexual violence at the cathedral choir's schools, 67 of them sexual violence, by 49 perpetrators (9 sexual). The worst violence was at the preparatory school in Etterzhausen and Pielenhofen. The report faulted Georg Ratzinger, choir director 1964–1994, for failing to intervene; he denied knowing of sexual abuse.
cases.cite: Ulrich Weber, Abschlussbericht zu Gewalt und Missbrauch bei den Regensburger Domspatzen, 18 July 2017

cases.n: Canisius-Kolleg Berlin and Jesuit schools
cases.who: Society of Jesus (Jesuits), Canisius-Kolleg Berlin and St. Blasien
cases.cover: Superiors helped one admitted abuser, Fr Wolfgang S., emigrate to South America; offences time-barred
cases.d: Former pupils told the headmaster of the Jesuit Canisius-Kolleg in 2004–2005 that two former teachers had abused them; after further reports in 2009–2010 the headmaster wrote to all former pupils in January 2010 and many more came forward, opening the German church scandal. The teachers could not be prosecuted because of time limits. A Jesuit, Fr Wolfgang S., admitted abusing pupils at St. Blasien in 1982–1984; the Jesuits said superiors helped him emigrate to South America.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Germany, citing Der Spiegel and Jesuit statements (2010)

cases.n: Cardinal Groër affair and Klasnic victims' commission, Austria
cases.victims_note: By 31 August 2021, payments approved in 2,550 cases (cases not necessarily individual people); about €33 million awarded
cases.who: Archdiocese of Vienna; Austrian Bishops' Conference; Independent Victims' Protection Commission (Klasnic Commission)
cases.d: Archbishop of Vienna Cardinal Hans Hermann Groër stepped down in September 1995 after a former pupil, followed by others and some monks, accused him of sexual abuse; church authorities confirmed the allegations in February 1998 and he withdrew from public life. In spring 2010 the bishops set up the Independent Victims' Protection Commission chaired by Waltraud Klasnic. By 31 August 2021 it had approved payments in 2,550 cases, about €33 million in total. At Kremsmünster Abbey school, former director Alfons Mandorfer was jailed for 12 years in 2013 for abusing 24 pupils.
cases.cite: Unabhängige Opferschutzkommission / Stiftung Opferschutz figures, as summarised in German Wikipedia

cases.n: CIASE (Sauvé Commission) — Catholic Church in France
cases.victims_note: Estimate from a population survey: about 216,000 abused by clergy and religious; more than 330,000 including lay church workers
cases.who: Catholic Church in France (commissioned by bishops and religious orders)
cases.cover: Commission called the abuse 'massive' and 'systemic' and said the church must accept institutional responsibility
cases.d: The Independent Commission on Sexual Abuse in the Church, chaired by Jean-Marc Sauvé, reported on 5 October 2021. Using a population survey, it estimated about 216,000 people were abused as minors by clergy and religious since 1950, and over 330,000 including lay workers in church institutions. It estimated 2,900–3,200 abusers, about 3% of clergy, and called the phenomenon systemic.
cases.cite: Commission indépendante sur les abus sexuels dans l'Église (CIASE), final report, 5 October 2021

cases.n: Bernard Preynat and Cardinal Barbarin, Lyon
cases.victims_note: Accused of abusing about 80 Boy Scouts; 10 victims were civil parties in the 2020 trial
cases.who: Archdiocese of Lyon; Fr Bernard Preynat; Cardinal Philippe Barbarin
cases.cover: Cardinal Barbarin convicted in March 2019 of failing to report abuse (suspended six months), cleared on appeal and by France's highest court in April 2021
cases.d: Fr Bernard Preynat was accused of abusing about 80 Boy Scouts between 1971 and 1991. He was laicised by the Holy See on 5 July 2019 and on 16 March 2020 a Lyon court sentenced him to five years in prison. Cardinal Philippe Barbarin was convicted on 7 March 2019 of not reporting the abuse and given a six-month suspended sentence; the conviction was overturned on appeal and the Cour de cassation cleared him in April 2021. Pope Francis accepted his resignation on 6 March 2020.
cases.cite: Lyon Tribunal correctionnel, 16 March 2020; Wikipedia, Bernard Preynat

cases.n: Spanish Ombudsman report on Church abuse
cases.victims_note: Survey estimate: 200,000 to 440,000 victims since 1940 (upper figure includes lay church workers)
cases.who: Catholic Church in Spain
cases.d: Spain's first official inquiry into clergy abuse, an 800-page report by Ombudsman Ángel Gabilondo released in October 2023, included a population survey indicating 200,000 to 440,000 potential victims since 1940. Separately, Spain's Supreme Court in April 2019 upheld a 17-year-seven-month sentence for Fr José Fernández for abusing two 12-year-old boys, and complaints against Marist school teachers in Barcelona rose to 43 against 12 teachers by February 2019.
cases.cite: Defensor del Pueblo, 'Informe sobre los abusos sexuales en el ámbito de la Iglesia católica', October 2023, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: University of Zurich pilot study — Catholic Church in Switzerland
cases.who: Swiss Bishops' Conference and religious orders (commissioned study)
cases.d: Historians at the University of Zurich, commissioned by the Swiss Bishops' Conference, published a pilot study in September 2023 on abuse in the Swiss Catholic Church since 1950. Its detailed figures could not be verified from a source opened for this dataset; see notes.
cases.cite: University of Zurich, Pilotprojekt zur Geschichte sexuellen Missbrauchs im Umfeld der römisch-katholischen Kirche in der Schweiz seit Mitte des 20. Jahrhunderts, September 2023 (figures unverified here)

cases.n: Independent Commission — Catholic Church in Portugal
cases.victims_note: 'At least 4,815' children abused since 1950 (commission's minimum estimate)
cases.who: Catholic Church in Portugal (commission set up by the bishops)
cases.d: An independent commission set up by the Portuguese bishops reported in February 2023 that at least 4,815 children had been abused by clergy and others in the church since 1950.
cases.cite: Comissão Independente para o Estudo dos Abusos Sexuais de Crianças na Igreja Católica Portuguesa, report of 13 February 2023, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Poland — bishops' 2019 figures, Sekielski films and sanctions on bishops
cases.victims_note: Church count: 625 children reported 1990–mid 2018; critics say an underestimate
cases.who: Polish Episcopal Conference; Archbishop Sławoj Leszek Głódź; Bishop Edward Janiak; Cardinal Henryk Gulbinowicz
cases.cover: Bishops sanctioned by the Vatican for protecting abusers: Janiak (Kalisz) ordered to resign June 2020; Głódź (Gdańsk) removed August 2020 after covering up abuse by Henryk Jankowski and Franciszek Cybula
cases.d: On 14 April 2019 the Polish Episcopal Conference reported about 382 priests accused of abusing 625 children between 1990 and mid-2018. The Sekielski brothers' documentaries 'Tell No One' (2019, 8.1 million YouTube views in days) and 'Hide and Seek' (2020) led the Vatican to investigate bishops. Pope Francis ordered Bishop Edward Janiak to resign in June 2020 for protecting abusive priests, removed Archbishop Głódź in August 2020, and in November 2020 sanctioned Cardinal Gulbinowicz. In May 2019 Poland raised the maximum sentence for child sexual abuse to 30 years.
cases.cite: Polish Episcopal Conference statistics, 14 April 2019; Holy See nunciature statements 2020, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Antonio Provolo Institute for the Deaf, Verona
cases.victims_note: 65 former students signed statements in 2010 that they or others were abused
cases.who: Compagnia di Maria per l'educazione dei sordomuti (Provolo Institute); Diocese of Verona
cases.cover: Fr Nicola Corradi, accused in Verona in 2009 and flagged by the diocese in 2011, was working at the institute's branch in Argentina, where he went on to abuse children
cases.d: In 2010 three former students of the Verona school for deaf children went public and 65 former students signed statements that they or others had been abused by 24 priests and religious from the 1950s to the 1980s. Fr Nicola Corradi was first accused in Verona in 2009 and flagged by the diocese in 2011, but continued working at the Provolo school in Argentina, where he was arrested in 2016 and later convicted.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Antonio Provolo Institute for the Deaf; Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Europe

cases.n: Próvolo Institute, Luján de Cuyo (Mendoza) — convictions 2019
cases.who: Provolo Institute for the Deaf (Argentina branch); Fr Nicola Corradi, Fr Horacio Corbacho, gardener Armando Gómez; Sr Kumiko Kosaka charged
cases.cover: Corradi had been accused in Verona in 2009 yet continued at the Argentine school; Japanese nun Kumiko Kosaka charged with abuse and covering up
cases.d: Priests Nicola Corradi (Italian) and Horacio Corbacho and other staff of the Provolo school for deaf children in Mendoza were arrested in 2016. On 25 November 2019 a Mendoza court convicted Corradi and Corbacho of sexually abusing 22 children, sentencing them to 42 and 45 years; gardener Armando Gómez received 18 years. Nun Kumiko Kosaka was charged in 2017 with abuse and cover-up.
cases.cite: Mendoza criminal court verdict, 25 November 2019, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Fr Julio César Grassi — Happy Children Foundation
cases.who: Fr Julio César Grassi, Fundación Felices los Niños
cases.d: Fr Julio César Grassi, who ran a foundation for poor children, was convicted by Oral Criminal Court 1 of Morón of one count of sexual abuse and one of corrupting a minor and sentenced to 15 years. He maintained his innocence and appealed.
cases.cite: Morón Oral Criminal Court 1 verdict (2009), as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Fr Alfonso Pedrajas diary — Jesuits in Bolivia
cases.victims_note: Admitted in his private diary to abusing more than 80 (about 85) minors
cases.who: Society of Jesus (Jesuits) in Bolivia
cases.cover: Confessed to his instructor in 1978, who covered it up; El País reported seven provincial superiors and about ten Bolivian and Spanish clerics covered for him
cases.d: Spanish Jesuit Alfonso Pedrajas (1943–2009) worked at Jesuit schools in Bolivia including the Juan XXIII boarding school in Cochabamba, which he later directed. His diary, published by El País on 30 April 2023, records that he abused more than 80 minors in the 1970s and 1980s. He confessed to a Jesuit superior in 1978; El País reported that seven provincial superiors and about ten clerics covered for him. He died in 2009 and was never prosecuted.
cases.cite: El País, 'Diario de un cura pederasta', 30 April 2023, as summarised by Spanish Wikipedia

cases.n: Fernando Karadima, Bishop Barros and Chile's bishops' resignation offer
cases.who: Archdiocese of Santiago; Fr Fernando Karadima; Bishop Juan Barros; Cardinals Errázuriz and Ezzati
cases.cover: Parishioners reported Karadima to Archbishop Fresno in 1984; Cardinal Errázuriz shelved a credible 2004–05 investigation; Barros, a Karadima protégé, made bishop of Osorno in 2015
cases.d: Parishioners first reported Fr Fernando Karadima to Archbishop Fresno in 1984. The Vatican found him guilty of abusing minors on 16 January 2011 and Pope Francis laicised him on 28 September 2018. After defending Bishop Juan Barros in January 2018, Francis sent Archbishop Charles Scicluna and Jordi Bertomeu to investigate; in an 8 April 2018 letter he admitted 'serious mistakes' of judgement. All 34 bishops at a May 2018 meeting in Rome offered their resignations; seven, including Barros, had been accepted by September 2018. Courts ordered the archdiocese to pay damages to survivors in 2018–2019.
cases.cite: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith verdict 2011; Pope Francis letter to the bishops of Chile, 8 April 2018; Wikipedia

cases.n: Marist Brothers Chile — Brother Abel Pérez
cases.victims_note: 'At least 14' minors per the order
cases.who: Marist Brothers in Chile
cases.cover: After confessing to superiors in 2010, Pérez was transferred to Peru
cases.d: In 2017 the Chilean Marist Brothers acknowledged that Brother Abel Pérez abused at least 14 minors between the 1970s and 2000. He had confessed to superiors in 2010 and was then transferred to Peru. Police investigated complaints at many of the order's schools.
cases.cite: Marist Brothers Chile statement 2017, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Sodalicio de Vida Cristiana — suppressed by the Vatican 2025
cases.who: Sodalitium Christianae Vitae; founder Luis Fernando Figari
cases.cover: Abuse reported by journalists in 2015 after years of internal silence; journalists faced legal action; Vatican commission in 2023 led to mass expulsions
cases.d: Journalists Pedro Salinas and Paola Ugaz exposed abuse by founder Luis Fernando Figari and associates in the 2015 book 'Mitad monjes, mitad soldados'. Investigators commissioned by the group in 2016 concluded Figari and former members sexually abused minors and adults; in February 2017 the group gave Peruvian prosecutors information on abuse of minors by Figari and four former members, and the Vatican barred Figari from contact with members. After a 2023 mission by Archbishop Scicluna and Mgr Bertomeu, Figari was expelled in August 2024 and over a dozen others, including a bishop, in September–October 2024. Pope Francis signed a decree suppressing the Sodalitium on 14 January 2025.
cases.cite: Sodalitium-commissioned investigators' reports 2016–17; Holy See decrees 2024–25, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Marcial Maciel and the Legion of Christ — 2019 internal report
cases.victims_note: Legion acknowledged 175 minors abused 1941–2019, 60 of them by Maciel
cases.who: Legion of Christ (Legionaries); founder Marcial Maciel
cases.cover: Letters to the Vatican in 1976, 1978 and 1989 and formal charges in 1998 produced no action; Vatican in 2010 said the Legion had shielded Maciel; Maciel never laicised or tried
cases.d: Former seminarians said Maciel abused them in Spain and Rome in the 1940s–50s; a victim and a bishop wrote to the Vatican in 1976 and 1978, and formal charges were filed in 1998, but no trial followed. In May 2006 the Vatican ordered Maciel to a life of prayer and penance, and on 1 May 2010 it called his conduct 'true crimes' and said the Legion had shielded him. The Legion's own report of 21 December 2019 acknowledged 175 minors abused from 1941 to 2019: 60 by Maciel and the rest by 33 priests, 14 of whom had themselves been abused within the order.
cases.cite: Legion of Christ, report on abuse 1941–2019, 21 December 2019; Holy See communiqué 1 May 2010, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Mexican bishops' conference — 426 priests investigated
cases.who: Conferencia del Episcopado Mexicano
cases.cover: El Universal reported only six convictions out of 156 alleged abuse cases involving minors, 2009–2019
cases.d: In January 2020 the Mexican Episcopal Conference said it had investigated 426 priests over the previous ten years for sexual abuse of minors and other crimes, and that 217 had been removed. El Universal reported on 2 February 2020 that only six of 156 alleged abuse cases involving minors from 2009 to 2019 ended in conviction.
cases.cite: Conferencia del Episcopado Mexicano statement, January 2020; El Universal, 2 February 2020, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Venezuela — priests accused or convicted 2001–2022
cases.who: Catholic Church in Venezuela
cases.cover: Three of the priests served little or no sentence and returned to ministry
cases.d: A 2022 Washington Post investigation found at least 10 Catholic priests accused or convicted of sexual abuse in Venezuela between 2001 and 2022, with complaints in at least eleven states. Three served little or no sentence and returned to the priesthood. The church confirmed the report's accuracy and announced an investigation.
cases.cite: Washington Post, 2022, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Brazil — priest convictions
cases.who: Catholic dioceses in Brazil
cases.d: In 2005 Fr Tarcísio Tadeu Spricigo and Fr Geraldo da Consolação Machado were convicted of child molestation in Brazil. Fr Felix Barbosa Carreiro was arrested and charged in Maranhão after police found him in a hotel room with four teenage boys. No national inquiry has been held in Brazil, the country with the world's largest Catholic population.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Latin America

cases.n: Crimen sollicitationis — secrecy instruction (1962)
cases.who: Holy See — Holy Office (now Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith)
cases.cover: Church proceedings to be kept absolutely confidential under automatic excommunication, binding tribunal members, accusers and witnesses
cases.d: The Holy Office instruction Crimen sollicitationis, approved by Pope John XXIII on 16 March 1962 and restating a 1922 instruction, governed canonical cases of solicitation in confession and also obscene acts with pre-adolescent children. It required absolute secrecy under pain of automatic excommunication. Many bishops did not know it was in their archives until press reports in 2003. Canon lawyer Thomas Doyle called the secrecy rules 'an explicit written policy to cover up cases', while others argue it did not bar reporting to police. It stayed in force until 2001.
cases.cite: Holy Office, Instructio de modo procedendi in causis sollicitationis, 1962, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Sacramentorum sanctitatis tutela / De delictis gravioribus (2001)
cases.who: Holy See — Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith (Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger, prefect)
cases.cover: All abuse-of-minor cases reserved to the CDF under pontifical secret
cases.d: Pope John Paul II's motu proprio Sacramentorum sanctitatis tutela (30 April 2001), with the CDF letter De delictis gravioribus of 18 May 2001, classed sexual abuse of a minor by a cleric as a graver delict and required that cases be sent to the CDF, then led by Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger. Cases were handled under pontifical secret until December 2019. The Holy See told the UN Committee against Torture in 2014 that 3,420 abuse cases had been investigated in the previous decade and 884 priests removed.
cases.cite: Sacramentorum sanctitatis tutela, 30 April 2001; Holy See to UN Committee against Torture, 2014, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Benedict XVI Pastoral Letter to the Catholics of Ireland (2010)
cases.who: Pope Benedict XVI
cases.d: In March 2010, after the Ryan and Murphy reports, Pope Benedict XVI issued a pastoral letter to Irish Catholics addressed in part to abuse survivors, acknowledging that nothing could undo the harm done to them. Critics said it did not address systemic failures. Benedict said in 2010 that about 400 priests had been laicised over a two-year period.
cases.cite: Pastoral Letter of the Holy Father Pope Benedict XVI to the Catholics of Ireland, 19 March 2010, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: UN Committee on the Rights of the Child — Holy See review (2014)
cases.who: Holy See
cases.cover: Committee found abusive clergy were reassigned without police notification, bishops not required to report to civil authorities, and a code of silence
cases.d: In February 2014 the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child found the Holy See had not taken sufficient measures against clerical abuse and had adopted practices that led to impunity. It said abusers were often moved to other parishes or countries without police being told, that bishops were not obliged to report to civil authorities, and that a code of silence meant cases were 'hardly ever reported'. In 2013 the committee had asked the Holy See for abuse data.
cases.cite: UN Committee on the Rights of the Child, Concluding observations on the second periodic report of the Holy See, CRC/C/VAT/CO/2, February 2014, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Pope Francis' letter to Chile's bishops and the Scicluna mission (2018)
cases.who: Pope Francis; Archbishop Charles Scicluna; Mgr Jordi Bertomeu
cases.d: After defending Bishop Juan Barros in January 2018, Pope Francis sent Archbishop Charles Scicluna and Jordi Bertomeu to take testimony in New York and Chile in February 2018. In a letter of 8 April 2018 he wrote that he had made 'serious mistakes in the assessment and perception of the situation' and summoned the Chilean bishops to Rome, where all of them offered to resign in May 2018.
cases.cite: Pope Francis, Letter to the Bishops of Chile, 8 April 2018, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Vos estis lux mundi (2019) and February 2019 summit
cases.who: Pope Francis
cases.d: Three months after a February 2019 Vatican summit of bishops' conference presidents on abuse, Pope Francis signed Vos estis lux mundi on 7 May 2019. It requires clerics and religious to report suspected abuse and cover-ups to church authorities and lets bishops be investigated for cover-up, but does not require reporting to civil authorities. It was made permanent on 30 April 2023.
cases.cite: Apostolic letter motu proprio Vos estis lux mundi, 7 May 2019, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Pontifical secret lifted for abuse cases (December 2019)
cases.who: Pope Francis
cases.d: On 17 December 2019 Pope Francis issued the instruction 'On the confidentiality of legal proceedings', removing the pontifical secret from cases of sexual abuse of minors and vulnerable persons, child sexual abuse material involving under-18s, and concealment of such crimes. Documents remain non-public but may be shared with civil authorities with jurisdiction.
cases.cite: Rescriptum ex audientia, 17 December 2019, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: McCarrick Report (Holy See, November 2020)
cases.who: Holy See; former Cardinal Theodore McCarrick
cases.cover: A 1999 warning letter reached Pope John Paul II; an inquiry stalled after three of four US bishops gave 'inaccurate and incomplete information'; McCarrick was promoted to Washington in 2000
cases.d: The Holy See's report of 10 November 2020 found that Pope John Paul II learned of allegations against Theodore McCarrick through a 1999 letter from Cardinal O'Connor but appointed him Archbishop of Washington after McCarrick denied them in writing. It faulted Benedict XVI for not stopping his influence and said Francis learned of allegations involving minors only in 2018. McCarrick was found guilty by the CDF and laicised on 16 February 2019. A Massachusetts charge of assaulting a 16-year-old in 1974 did not go to trial after he was ruled incompetent in 2023; he died in April 2025.
cases.cite: Secretariat of State, Report on the Holy See's Institutional Knowledge and Decision-Making Related to Former Cardinal Theodore Edgar McCarrick, 10 November 2020

cases.n: Nuncio Józef Wesołowski and Fr Wojciech Gil — Dominican Republic
cases.who: Apostolic Nunciature in the Dominican Republic; Archbishop Józef Wesołowski; Fr Wojciech Gil
cases.cover: Wesołowski recalled to the Vatican in August 2013 before Dominican authorities opened an investigation; Gil returned to Poland, which has no extradition treaty with the Dominican Republic
cases.d: Polish Archbishop Józef Wesołowski, papal nuncio to the Dominican Republic from 2008, was recalled in August 2013 amid allegations of abusing minors; Dominican authorities opened an investigation in September 2013. The Vatican laicised him in June 2014 and indicted him in June 2015 for possessing child abuse images, but he died on 27 August 2015 before trial. Fr Wojciech Gil, who worked at the nunciature, returned to Poland; using Dominican evidence, Polish police arrested him in February 2014 and he was sentenced to seven years in March 2015.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Józef Wesołowski, citing Vatican and Dominican statements and Polish court reporting

cases.n: Vatican tribunal — diplomat Carlo Capella and the Martinelli trial
cases.who: Holy See diplomat Mgr Carlo Capella; St Pius X pre-seminary
cases.d: On 23 June 2018 a Vatican City court convicted former Holy See diplomat Carlo Capella, recalled from the Washington nunciature, of possessing child abuse images and sentenced him to five years. On 14 October 2020 the first Vatican criminal trial for sexual abuse began, of Fr Gabriele Martinelli over abuse at the pre-seminary for altar boys inside the Vatican, with a former rector charged with aiding and abetting.
cases.cite: Vatican City State tribunal, 23 June 2018; Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases by country

cases.n: Fr Brendan Smyth — Norbertine order
cases.victims_note: At least 143 children
cases.who: Norbertine order (Kilnacrott Abbey); Fr Brendan Smyth
cases.cover: Norbertines moved him between parishes, dioceses and countries without reporting him; at a 1975 church inquiry two boys signed oaths of silence; mishandled extradition by the Irish Attorney General's office contributed to the fall of the government in 1994
cases.d: Norbertine priest Brendan Smyth abused at least 143 children over more than 40 years in Belfast, Dublin and the United States (Rhode Island, North Dakota, Boston). In 1975 Seán Brady, later Cardinal, witnessed two boys sign oaths of silence during a church inquiry; police were not told. After his 1991 arrest he hid in the Republic for three years; the handling of the RUC's extradition request contributed to the collapse of the Irish government in December 1994. He was convicted in Belfast in 1994 and in Dublin in 1997 (74 counts, 12 years) and died in prison in August 1997.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Brendan Smyth, citing court records and Irish press

cases.n: Diocese of Raphoe — Fr Eugene Greene
cases.who: Catholic Diocese of Raphoe
cases.d: While Séamus Hegarty was Bishop of Raphoe (1982–1994), Fr Eugene Greene raped 26 young people. Greene was arrested in 1999 and in 2000 pleaded guilty to 40 of 115 charges, receiving 12 years. Four more Raphoe priests were convicted of sex abuse in 2011.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Ireland

cases.n: Catholic Boy Scouts of Ireland — review 2020
cases.victims_note: 275 known or suspected abusers shielded by CBSI and the Scout Association of Ireland combined
cases.who: Catholic Boy Scouts of Ireland (with Scout Association of Ireland), now Scouting Ireland
cases.cover: Organisations shielded known or suspected abusers after abuse was reported
cases.d: A review published in May 2020 found that over several decades before their 2004 merger into Scouting Ireland, the Catholic Boy Scouts of Ireland and the Scout Association of Ireland shielded 275 known or suspected abusers. Scouting Ireland accepted the findings and apologised.
cases.cite: Scouting Ireland historical abuse review, May 2020, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Northern Ireland Historical Institutional Abuse Inquiry — Catholic homes
cases.who: Sisters of Nazareth (Nazareth House and Nazareth Lodge), De La Salle Brothers (Rubane House), Good Shepherd Sisters, Sisters of St Louis; Diocese of Down and Connor
cases.d: The inquiry chaired by Sir Anthony Hart reported on 20 January 2017, finding 'shocking levels of sexual, physical and emotional abuse' in children's homes from 1922 to 1995. Modules covered the Sisters of Nazareth homes in Derry and Belfast, the De La Salle home at Rubane House, Good Shepherd institutions and Fr Brendan Smyth, and the child migrant scheme that sent children to Australia. It recommended compensation and an apology, made in the Assembly on 11 March 2022.
cases.cite: Historical Institutional Abuse Inquiry report, 20 January 2017

cases.n: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry — Sisters of Nazareth
cases.victims_note: Police received more than 300 complaints from former residents
cases.who: Poor Sisters of Nazareth
cases.d: The Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry found in May 2019 that children in Nazareth House orphanages from 1933 to 1984 suffered sexual abuse 'of the utmost depravity'. Police received more than 300 complaints. In 2025 the Sisters agreed to pay up to £5.75 million to survivors and three former staff were convicted.
cases.cite: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry, Case Study no. 2 findings (Nazareth Houses), 2019

cases.n: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry — Smyllum Park and Bellevue (Daughters of Charity)
cases.who: Daughters of Charity of St Vincent de Paul
cases.d: About 11,600 children passed through Smyllum Park orphanage, run by the Daughters of Charity from 1864 to 1981. The inquiry's October 2018 findings said children were sexually abused by priests, a trainee priest, sisters, staff and a volunteer, and beaten with implements. Seventeen people were later charged; in 2025 the order agreed to pay up to £10 million.
cases.cite: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry, Case Study no. 1 findings (Daughters of Charity), October 2018

cases.n: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry — Fort Augustus Abbey and Carlekemp (Benedictines)
cases.who: English Benedictine Congregation — Fort Augustus Abbey School and Carlekemp Priory School
cases.cover: Complaints to senior monks were inadequately handled; after one complaint the school did not tell police and sent the monk, Denis Chrysostom Alexander, back to Australia
cases.d: In August 2021 the Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry found both Benedictine schools were 'havens for paedophiles' with sexual abuse over many years. A 2013 BBC programme had presented evidence against seven monks. Denis Chrysostom Alexander, sent back to Australia after parents complained, was arrested in Sydney in 2017 and pleaded guilty in 2021; Robert MacKenzie was extradited from Canada in 2020 but the case was dropped in 2021.
cases.cite: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry, Case Study findings on Benedictine establishments, August 2021; BBC Scotland 'Sins of Our Fathers' 2013

cases.n: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry — Marist and Christian Brothers schools
cases.victims_note: St Ninian's convictions in 2016 concerned 35 boys
cases.who: Marist Brothers (St Joseph's College Dumfries, St Columba's College Largs); Christian Brothers (St Ninian's, Falkland)
cases.d: The inquiry found in February 2021 that the Christian Brothers' St Ninian's school in Falkland was 'a place of abuse and deprivation', especially 1969–1983; two Brothers were jailed in 2016 for abuse of 35 boys across more than 100 charges. It found abuse at the Marist Brothers' schools in Dumfries and Largs between 1951 and 1980 'shocking and distressing'; the Marists apologised in November 2021.
cases.cite: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry, findings on Christian Brothers (Feb 2021) and Marist Brothers (2021)

cases.n: Fr Paul Moore — moved by his bishop to Toronto
cases.victims_note: Three children (1977–1981) and a student priest (1995)
cases.who: Diocese of Galloway; Bishop Maurice Taylor
cases.cover: Bishop Maurice Taylor sent Moore to Toronto and Fort Augustus
cases.d: Fr Paul Moore was convicted in 2018 of abusing three children between 1977 and 1981 and a student priest in 1995. Bishop Maurice Taylor had sent him to Toronto, Canada and to Fort Augustus.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases by country (Scotland), citing BBC

cases.n: Indian Residential Schools run by Catholic entities — TRC and papal apology
cases.place: Maskwacis, Alberta (site of the 2022 papal apology)
cases.victims_note: About 150,000 children attended residential schools; 31,970 sexual or serious assault claims resolved through the Independent Assessment Process (all denominations)
cases.who: Catholic dioceses and orders (incl. Oblates of Mary Immaculate) that ran about 44 of 80 schools at the 1931 peak (TRC says about 70% overall)
cases.cover: Federal government funded and mandated attendance; Catholic entities cited lack of funds to compensate
cases.d: About 150,000 Indigenous children were sent to Canada's residential schools; at the 1931 peak 44 of 80 were run by Catholic dioceses and orders. The Truth and Reconciliation Commission's 2015 report called the system cultural genocide; the Independent Assessment Process resolved 31,970 claims of sexual or serious physical assault. Oblates faced more than 2,000 lawsuits in western provinces. In July 2022 Pope Francis apologised at Maskwacis for 'the evil committed by so many Christians'.
cases.cite: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada, Final Report, December 2015; Wikipedia, Canadian Indian residential school system

cases.n: Basilian Fathers — Canadian convictions
cases.who: Congregation of St. Basil (Basilian Fathers)
cases.d: Basilian priest William Hodgson Marshall pleaded guilty in 2011 to 16 counts of indecent assault and one of sexual assault from 1952–1986 in Windsor, Toronto and Sudbury schools. Robert Whyte pleaded guilty in 1990 to abusing 18 children (1962–1982); Kenneth O'Keefe received house arrest in 2012–2013. In April 2020 the Supreme Court of Canada let stand an award of over $2.5 million, including $500,000 punitive damages, against the Basilians.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Canada, citing court rulings

cases.n: Fr Eric Dejaeger — Oblate in Nunavut
cases.who: Missionary Oblates of Mary Immaculate; Belgian-born Fr Eric Dejaeger
cases.d: Belgian-born Oblate Eric Dejaeger was convicted on 12 September 2014 of 24 counts of indecent assault and other sexual offences against Inuit children in Igloolik, Nunavut, between 1978 and 1982. He had earlier been convicted of 11 counts of sexual and indecent assault against children at his previous post in Baker Lake.
cases.cite: Nunavut Court of Justice, 2014, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Archdiocese of Los Angeles — settlements 2007 and 2024
cases.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Los Angeles; Cardinal Roger Mahony
cases.cover: In 2013 Archbishop Gómez removed Cardinal Mahony from public duties over his handling of abusive clergy
cases.d: The Archdiocese of Los Angeles agreed a $660 million settlement with 508 victims in 2007 and, in October 2024, an $880 million settlement with 1,350 victims, the largest by any US diocese; total payouts reached about $1.5 billion. In February 2013 Archbishop José Gómez barred Cardinal Roger Mahony from public ministry over his handling of abusers.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Sexual abuse scandal in the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Los Angeles

cases.n: Diocese of Stockton — Fr Oliver O'Grady
cases.victims_note: Admitted in 2005 to abusing at least 25 children
cases.who: Diocese of Stockton; Bishop Roger Mahony (later Cardinal Archbishop of Los Angeles)
cases.cover: Bishop Mahony ordered him away from one family in 1980, then moved him to a new parish in 1984 before a psychiatric evaluation was complete
cases.d: Irish-born priest Oliver O'Grady, ordained in 1971 for the Diocese of Stockton, abused children from about 1973 and was moved between parishes. Bishop Roger Mahony knew of concerns by 1980 and moved him in 1984. O'Grady was convicted in 1993 and sentenced to 14 years; a 1998 civil jury awarded $30 million (reduced to $7 million). Paroled and deported to Ireland in 2000, he was convicted there for child abuse images in 2012 and 2020.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Oliver O'Grady, citing court records

cases.n: Diocese of Lafayette — Gilbert Gauthe (first national case)
cases.who: Diocese of Lafayette; Fr Gilbert Gauthe
cases.cover: Bishop assigned him as Boy Scout chaplain in 1974 despite allegations; sent for therapy in 1976 and returned
cases.d: Fr Gilbert Gauthe admitted abusing 37 children while serving in the Diocese of Lafayette from 1972 to 1983. In 1974 the bishop made him a Boy Scout chaplain despite allegations about altar boys. In October 1985 he pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 20 years; the diocese paid more than $20 million. His 1984–85 case was the first widely publicised clergy abuse prosecution in the US.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Gilbert Gauthe

cases.n: US diocesan bankruptcies and settlements
cases.victims_note: About 17,000 victims paid about $4 billion since the 1980s (Wikipedia summary); BishopAccountability reported more than $3 billion by 2012
cases.who: US Catholic dioceses (Portland, Tucson, Spokane, San Diego, Davenport, Milwaukee, Albany and others)
cases.cover: Milwaukee: Cardinal Timothy Dolan, with Vatican approval, moved $57 million into a cemetery trust, which kept it from victims; released files showed priests moved without telling police
cases.d: Starting with Portland in 2004, at least 13 US dioceses filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy by 2023 under abuse claims. US dioceses have paid about $4 billion to roughly 17,000 victims since the 1980s. In Milwaukee, which filed in 2011 after paying $29 million on about 200 cases, released documents showed abusive priests were moved between assignments without notifying law enforcement.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic sexual abuse scandal in the United States

cases.n: Christian Brothers in Australia — Ballarat and WA orphanages
cases.place: Ballarat (St Alipius, St Patrick's); Bindoon, Clontarf, Castledare, Tardun (WA)
cases.victims_note: 853 children (Ballarat region claims); 22% of Brothers in Australia alleged perpetrators since 1950
cases.who: Congregation of Christian Brothers
cases.cover: Convicted Brothers Dowlan and Best were moved from junior to senior campus and continued offending; leaders knew of abuse at WA orphanages for decades
cases.d: The Royal Commission found 22% of Christian Brothers in Australia had been alleged perpetrators since 1950, and that claims concerning 853 children, against 281 Brothers, led to A$37.3 million in compensation. In Ballarat Brothers Best and Dowlan were moved between campuses and kept offending. From 1980 to 2015 the Christian Brothers made 763 payments totalling A$48.5 million, the most of any Catholic authority. Over 200 former residents of the WA orphanages, including child migrants, sued from 1993 and settled in 1996.
cases.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, final report Dec 2017; Wikipedia, Congregation of Christian Brothers

cases.n: Maitland-Newcastle diocese — Fletcher, Cunneen inquiry and Archbishop Wilson (acquitted)
cases.who: Diocese of Maitland-Newcastle; Archbishop Philip Wilson
cases.cover: Monsignor Cotter's letter about Fr Denis McAlinden said 'we do not think it can be real serious'
cases.d: A NSW Special Commission of Inquiry led by Margaret Cunneen, ordered in November 2012, reported on 30 May 2014 on church and police handling of abuse in the diocese; police Strike Force Lantle laid more than 170 charges. Archbishop of Adelaide Philip Wilson was found guilty on 22 May 2018 of failing to report abuse by Fr James Fletcher in 1976, but was acquitted on appeal on 6 December 2018. Fletcher died in jail in 2006.
cases.cite: Special Commission of Inquiry into matters relating to the Police investigation of certain child sexual abuse allegations in the Catholic Diocese of Maitland-Newcastle, 30 May 2014; NSW District Court 6 Dec 2018

cases.n: Marist Brothers in Australia
cases.who: Marist Brothers
cases.cover: Royal Commission found the order failed to act on complaints against a Brother at Marist College Ashgrove; a Brother pleaded guilty in 2020 to concealing abuse
cases.d: In June 2019 the Marist Brothers listed 154 members accused of abusing children in Australia between 1980 and 2015. The Royal Commission found the order's response worsened the harm and that many alleged abusers kept access to children for years. Brother William Wade was convicted in 2017 of abusing two boys and in 2020 pleaded guilty to concealing abuse.
cases.cite: Marist Brothers statement, June 2019; Royal Commission findings, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Marylands School and Hebron Trust — St John of God Brothers
cases.victims_note: 118 sex abuse allegations / over 120 complaints; 21 of 37 Brothers in Christchurch accused
cases.who: Brothers Hospitallers of St John of God
cases.cover: Brother Bernard McGrath was transferred to Australia after 1977 allegations and later put in charge of Hebron Trust; victims sometimes required to sign non-disclosure agreements
cases.d: Marylands, a Christchurch residential school for boys with learning disabilities run by the St John of God Brothers from 1955 to 1984, and the order's later Hebron Trust, were described by the Royal Commission in 2023 as 'hell on earth'. 21 of the 37 Brothers who served in Christchurch faced abuse allegations. Bernard McGrath, known to have offended from 1977, was convicted in NZ in 1993 and 2006 and extradited to Australia in 2014 to face 252 charges. The order's Australasian branch had paid NZ$5.1 million by 2006.
cases.cite: Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care, 'Stolen Lives, Marked Souls', July 2023; Wikipedia, Marylands School

cases.n: Marist Brothers and priests — New Zealand convictions
cases.who: Marist Brothers; Society of Mary
cases.d: A 2018 Otago Daily Times report listed nine Marist Brothers convicted of crimes against boys in New Zealand, including two at Hato Paora College. Marist priest Alan Woodcock was extradited from England and convicted in 2004 of 21 offences (1978–1987). Brother Kevin Healy was convicted in 2020. The church admitted in 2022 that 14% of its diocesan clergy had been accused since 1950.
cases.cite: Otago Daily Times 2018 and court reports, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Fiji — transferred clergy and Julian Fox
cases.victims_note: A 2020 report cited about 1,300 alleged child abuse cases in Fiji involving clergy, some from Australia and New Zealand (figure as reported, not an official finding)
cases.who: Salesians; Catholic Church in Fiji
cases.cover: Fox was transferred to Fiji in 1999 after Australian police began investigating; the Fiji church knew of allegations nine years before he was charged
cases.d: Salesian priest Julian Fox was moved to Fiji in 1999 after Australian police began investigating abuse allegations; he was jailed in Australia in 2015. The Catholic Church in Fiji knew of the allegations nine years before he was charged. In July 2020 1News reported that some of about 1,300 alleged child abuse cases involving clergy in Fiji concerned clergy from Australia and New Zealand.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Australia and New Zealand, citing 1News (July 2020)

cases.n: Richard Daschbach — Topu Honis shelter, Oecusse
cases.victims_note: Convicted for four girls; charges covered 14 cases; lawyers represented 17 victims
cases.who: Society of the Divine Word (SVD); US-born Fr Richard Daschbach
cases.d: US-born Divine Word missionary Richard Daschbach founded the Topu Honis children's shelter in Oecusse in 1991 and admitted abusing minors there between 1991 and 2012. The Vatican dismissed him from the priesthood (2018–2020). Timor-Leste prosecutors charged him with 14 counts in September 2020, and on 21 December 2021 a court convicted him of abusing four girls and sentenced him to 12 years. A 2020 Diocese of Dili report had disputed the allegations.
cases.cite: Oecusse District Court, 21 December 2021, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Bishop Carlos Ximenes Belo — Vatican sanctions
cases.who: Salesians; Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo (Nobel Peace laureate)
cases.cover: Vatican received allegations in 2019 and imposed sanctions in 2020 but did not disclose them until a magazine reported the case in 2022
cases.d: On 28 September 2022 Dutch magazine De Groene Amsterdammer reported that two men said Bishop Belo had abused them and other boys in Fatumaca and Dili, before and during his time as bishop. The next day the Vatican confirmed it had received allegations in 2019 and imposed disciplinary sanctions in 2020: limits on movement and ministry, no contact with minors and no contact with Timor-Leste. The sanctions were reinforced in 2021. Belo had left Timor in 2002 and worked in Maputo, Mozambique from 2004.
cases.cite: De Groene Amsterdammer, 28 September 2022; Holy See Press Office statement, 29 September 2022, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Kerala — priest convictions and Bishop Mulakkal acquittal
cases.who: Syro-Malabar and Latin dioceses in Kerala; Bishop Franco Mulakkal of Jalandhar
cases.d: Fr Robin Vadakkumchery of Kannur was arrested in 2017 for raping a 15-year-old girl who later gave birth, and was sentenced to 20 years by a POCSO court in 2019. In 2014 Fr Raju Kokkan of Thrissur was arrested for raping a nine-year-old, and three other Kerala priests were arrested on charges of raping minors. Bishop Franco Mulakkal, accused by an adult nun of rape between 2014 and 2016, was arrested on 21 September 2018 and acquitted of all charges on 14 January 2022; he resigned in 2023. In 2016 the Ootacamund diocese reappointed a convicted priest without safeguards.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Asia; Franco Mulakkal

cases.n: Philippines — priest arrests and removals
cases.place: Naval (Biliran), Cadiz City, Tuguegarao, Iloilo, Borongan
cases.victims_note: Includes at least 10 boys in the 2018 Naval, Biliran case
cases.who: Catholic dioceses in the Philippines; a US priest assigned in Biliran
cases.d: In 2018 an American priest assigned in the Philippines was arrested for abusing at least 10 boys in Naval, Biliran. Other cases include a priest arrested in Marikina (2017), a priest charged in Cadiz City with raping a four-year-old (2019), an arrest in Tuguegarao for abusing a 16-year-old (2022), and a Diocese of San Carlos priest arrested in March 2023 for raping a 17-year-old choir member. Pope Francis removed a Borongan priest on 10 May 2023. There has been no national inquiry in Asia's largest Catholic country.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Asia, citing Philippine press

cases.n: Indonesia — Syahril Parlindungan Marbun, altar boys
cases.victims_note: Police said the number may be higher
cases.who: Catholic parish (church volunteer Syahril Parlindungan Marbun)
cases.d: Police reported that Syahril Parlindungan Marbun abused 20 altar boys between 2002 and 2020, and said the number could be higher.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Asia, citing Indonesian police statements

cases.n: St Michael's School, Soni — Rosminian priests
cases.who: Institute of Charity (Rosminians); English priest Kit Cunningham and three others
cases.cover: The order knew of Cunningham's abuse before his death in 2010; it became public only through a BBC documentary in June 2011
cases.d: In the 1960s English Rosminian priest Kit Cunningham and three other priests abused boys at St Michael's boarding school in Soni, Tanzania. The order knew before Cunningham's death in 2010; the abuse became public in a BBC documentary on 21 June 2011. Former pupils sued in Leicester in March 2013, and the order's 2014–15 accounts show £1,746,523 in settlement and legal costs; it later apologised for the abuse and cover-up.
cases.cite: BBC, 'Abused: Breaking the Silence', 21 June 2011; Rosminian charity accounts 2015, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Kenya — RTÉ 'Mission to Prey' and false allegation against Fr Kevin Reynolds
cases.who: Irish missionaries in Kenya; RTÉ
cases.d: RTÉ's May 2011 documentary 'Mission to Prey' reported on clerical abuse by missionaries in Africa. It wrongly alleged that Irish priest Fr Kevin Reynolds had abused a girl and fathered a child in Kenya; paternity tests disproved this and RTÉ apologised and paid damages, a major Irish broadcasting scandal. Separately in 2011 a Dutch bishop was investigated over alleged abuse of a minor 18 years earlier when he was a priest in Ngong diocese, and was retired by the church.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Africa, citing RTÉ

cases.n: Mauritius — Irish missionary abuse and priest convictions
cases.who: Catholic Diocese of Port Louis; Irish priest at St Joseph's College
cases.d: A survivor has said he was abused at age 11 in the late 1950s by an Irish priest at St Joseph's College, Curepipe. In October 2019 Fr Joseph-Marie Moctee was sentenced to three years for abusing a 15-year-old in April 2015 at Chamarel. In September 2016 another priest was arrested over a complaint at St Louis Cathedral, Port Louis (complainant aged 20).
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Africa, citing Mauritian press

cases.n: Slovenia — Fr Franc Frantar
cases.victims_note: 'Up to 16' minors
cases.who: Archdiocese of Ljubljana; Fr Franc Frantar
cases.cover: Avoided prosecution by going to Malawi as a missionary until an Interpol notice was issued
cases.d: Slovenian priest Franc Frantar was detained in 2006 for abusing up to 16 minors and later sentenced (sources give three and a half and five years). He first avoided prosecution by going to Malawi as a missionary and returned to Slovenia after Interpol issued a notice.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Europe

cases.n: Croatia — first priest convictions
cases.victims_note: Čuček: 37 girls; Ljubičić: five teenage boys
cases.who: Catholic dioceses in Croatia
cases.cover: Nediljko Ivanov, whose abuse 1983–1991 was reported in 2012, was time-barred; a church court ordered only prayer, fasting and an apology and he continued to say Mass
cases.d: In 2000 Fr Ivan Čuček was convicted of abusing 37 girls; his three-year sentence was cut to 18 months by the Supreme Court. In 2007 Fr Drago Ljubičić of Rab became the first Croatian priest to serve prison time, three years for molesting five teenage boys. Fr Nediljko Ivanov of Bibinje became the first priest convicted by a Croatian church court, but civil prosecution was time-barred.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Europe and by country

cases.n: Czech Republic — Fr František Merta
cases.victims_note: More than 20 boys
cases.who: Archdiocese of Olomouc; Archbishop Jan Graubner (alleged failure to report)
cases.cover: Archbishop Graubner allegedly did not report him and moved him between parishes
cases.d: In 2000–2001 Fr František Merta was found guilty of abusing more than 20 boys and received a two-year suspended sentence. Archbishop Jan Graubner allegedly failed to report him and moved him between parishes when problems arose.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Europe

cases.n: Norway — Bishop Georg Müller of Trondheim
cases.who: Territorial Prelature of Trondheim; Bishop Georg Müller
cases.d: Former Bishop of Trondheim Georg Müller, who retired in 2009, admitted in 2010 that he had abused an altar boy in the 1980s. In April 2010 the church in Norway had reported 18 abuse cases; in Denmark 17 had been reported.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Europe

cases.n: Malta — St Joseph Home convictions
cases.victims_note: 84 allegations recorded by April 2010
cases.who: Missionary Society of St Paul (St Joseph Home); Maltese clergy
cases.d: By April 2010 the church in Malta had recorded 84 allegations. Fr Charles Pulis was sentenced to six years and Fr Godwin Scerri to five years for abusing boys at a church children's home; Donald Bellizzi received three years in 2020.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases by country (Malta)

cases.n: Belgium — Halsberghe commission (2000) and convictions
cases.victims_note: Over 300 complaints to the 2000 commission
cases.who: Catholic Church in Belgium
cases.cover: In about half the 32 upheld cases the accused refused to appear; 31 cases were time-barred and only one reached court; in June 2010 police seized 450 internal dossiers from the Mechelen archbishop's palace
cases.d: A church commission chaired by Godelieve Halsberghe from 2000 received over 300 complaints and upheld 32 of 33 formal ones; 31 were time-barred. Convictions included Fr Bruno Vos (nine years in 2009 for raping four minors), Robert Borremans (five years, 2008) and two Brothers jailed for ten years each in 2005 for abusing disabled people. On 24 June 2010 police raided the archbishop's palace in Mechelen, seizing 450 dossiers, and searched Cardinal Danneels' residence.
cases.cite: Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Belgium

cases.n: Italy — no national inquiry; Rete l'Abuso count
cases.victims_note: Rete l'Abuso: about 300 cases in the courts since 2000, 150–170 convictions (victims' group estimate)
cases.who: Catholic Church in Italy; Italian Bishops' Conference
cases.cover: In May 2012 the Italian Bishops' Conference said priests had no obligation to report suspected abuse to police
cases.d: Italy has no official statistics or national inquiry. The victims' network Rete l'Abuso counted about 300 cases of priests and nuns before Italian courts since 2000, with 150 to 170 convictions (October 2018). In May 2012 the Italian Bishops' Conference said its priests had no duty to report suspected abuse to police. Cases include Fr Mauro Galli (6 years 4 months, 2014) and a former Roman Rota judge who pleaded guilty to child abuse image offences in 2018.
cases.cite: Rete l'Abuso, 2018; Wikipedia, Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Italy

cases.n: Bishop Gustavo Zanchetta of Orán — convicted 2022
cases.place: San Ramón de la Nueva Orán, Salta
cases.victims_note: Two adult seminarians (not minors)
cases.who: Diocese of Orán; Bishop Gustavo Zanchetta
cases.cover: After resigning in 2017 amid complaints he was given a post at the Vatican's APSA in December 2017; suspended in January 2019
cases.d: Bishop Gustavo Zanchetta resigned from the Diocese of Orán in August 2017 amid complaints from clergy and was named an official at the Vatican's patrimony office (APSA) in December 2017. Argentine prosecutors charged him in June 2019 with sexually abusing two adult seminarians, and on 4 March 2022 a Salta court sentenced him to four and a half years. Included as a case of a bishop moved to the Vatican, though the victims were adults.
cases.cite: Salta court verdict, 4 March 2022, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Chile — Fr José Andrés Aguirre ('Cura Tato')
cases.who: Archdiocese of Santiago
cases.d: Fr José Andrés Aguirre Ovalle, known as 'Cura Tato', was found guilty of nine sexual abuse charges and sentenced to 12 years. A lower-court order for the church to pay damages was revoked by the Supreme Court. Chile removed the statute of limitations for child sexual abuse on 11 July 2019 (not retroactive).
cases.cite: Chilean court rulings, as summarised by Wikipedia

cases.n: Denis Chrysostom Alexander — extradition from Australia
cases.who: Benedictine monk, Fort Augustus Abbey School
cases.cover: Sent back to Australia by the school after parents complained; police not informed
